items.title: Flip Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996
items.q: In 1942, Flip added the tenor sax and was soon hired by Benny Goodman... [INTERVIEWER] You spent a little time touring with Benny Goodman too. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah.

ctx.x: The music, the jazz at the time, was it moving from Dixieland to swing? Was it kind of in the middle or can you describe it all?

Well it was swinging in those days, like I remember Benny Goodman was just starting out you know. He had the band at Billy Rose in New York. He wasn’t very popular yet you know, but he was a good player, and he had good bands and everything. But he wasn’t that popular until he made that tour to California. And there were a lot of good players.
